local_facts.claim: California separates a wrongful death action for eligible survivors under Code of Civil Procedure section 377.60 from a survival action that passes the decedent's own claim to a personal representative or, if none, a successor in interest under section 377.30. Section 377.34 generally excludes the decedent's pain, suffering, and disfigurement from survival damages, subject to statutory exceptions.
local_facts.why_it_matters: The people who lost a family member may have their own wrongful death claim, while a different person may need authority to bring the survival action. Keeping those paths separate changes who is included, what documents are needed, and which losses are being evaluated.
local_facts.title: California uses two different claim paths after a death

local_facts.claim: Fresno County Superior Court states that Unlimited Civil cases are heard at the B. F. Sisk Courthouse, 1130 O Street, Fresno, CA 93721.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A wrongful death case can require an Unlimited Civil filing, but venue depends on the case facts. When Fresno Superior Court is the correct venue, the court's civil division and filing location are concrete local details rather than an abstract reference to 'the courthouse.'
local_facts.title: Fresno's Unlimited Civil cases have a named filing location

local_facts.claim: A Fresno County economic study found that agricultural production and processing directly supported 63,103 jobs in 2023.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A local work death may involve a farm, packing operation, processor, labor contractor, transportation provider, equipment maker, or property owner. Preserving the employer, worksite, equipment, and coworker records early helps determine which relationships need to be examined.
local_facts.title: Agriculture and processing shape Fresno County work records

anchors.label: Classes of people who may assert the death claim
anchors.detail: Section 377.60 groups them into heirs at (a), dependents at (b), and a dependent minor of the household at (c).

anchors.label: Factors a judge may weigh on a fee paid from a minor's recovery
anchors.detail: Rule 7.955(b) lists fourteen, three of them specific to the risk, advanced costs and payment delay of a contingency.

fee_rows.stage: The percentage in a death case
fee_rows.note: No California statute limits it. Rule 1.5(a) prohibits an unconscionable or illegal fee and leaves the figure to be negotiated.

fee_rows.stage: The clause saying the rate is negotiable
fee_rows.note: Section 6147(a)(4) makes the written contract state that the fee is not fixed by law wherever section 6146 does not apply.

fee_rows.stage: The statutory percentages people confuse with this
fee_rows.note: The 25 and 33 percent limits in section 6146(a) apply solely to professional negligence claims against health care providers.
Section 377.60 lists a spouse, domestic partner, children and issue, intestate takers, dependent relatives, and a qualifying minor of the household.

fee_rows.stage: A fee paid out of a child's share
fee_rows.note: Rule 7.955(a)(1) applies a reasonable fee standard to money paid for a minor unless the court approved the agreement in advance.
Rule 7.952(a) requires the petitioner and the minor to attend unless the court dispenses with the appearance for good cause.
